title.narrative: The Young Women for Awareness, Agency, Advocacy, and Accountability (YW4A)

description.narrative: The programme aims to strengthen and diversify young women’s participation and amplify their voices to effectively influence decision-making towards gender-just laws, policies, norms, and practices related to their bodily integrity and equal participation.

The programme will achieve this through 4 main outcomes: 1.Strengthening the advocacy capacity of 27 women’s rights organizations (WROs) to amplify young women’s voices in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025.2.Enhancing the leadership of 17,540 young women to effectively engage in collective action and decision-making in public, private, and civic spaces in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025.3.Transforming social norms and practices of 22 faith-based organizations (FBOs) that constrain young women’s rights in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025. 4.Influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilisation and implementation of 18 laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya and South Sudan by 2025.

title.narrative: WRGE indicator 5.2.2: (WRG049y) IO2 Strengthened individual leadership of 13,700 young women across the four countries

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices. Leadership roles are measured by capacity to apply different forms of leadership training (to peers), willingness to become role models, self-confidence and efficacy, planning and facilitation skills, public speaking, advocacy, willingness to engage in policy change and with actors in public and civic decision-making spaces, exercise of leadership roles in the community, women’s groups, CSOs and political spaces, mobilization of young women, networking.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.2 (WRG049y) # of young women who have gained awareness of their rights, deepened their understanding of women's rights issues, and the ability to generate support around a common cause.

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices.

comment.narrative: Before the RiseUp! Training of Trainers started, 214 Cohort 1 young women took part in the Young Women Leadership (YWL) assessment as to measure their leadership capacity. The YWL score presents the young women's current capacity following the three classifications: Experienced, Aspiring, and Starting. The majority of young women were classified as "Aspiring" leaders. A smaller proportion were classified as "Experienced" leaders. The "Starting" category had the fewest YW, indicating limited conditions and no leadership experience. Marginalized young women followed a similar distribution, with a majority in the "Aspiring" category.

The Cohort 1 training target for 2021 was set at 214 young women. Apart from training the young women, the objectives were also to translate and localize the Rise Up! Training materials to the Palestinian context.
In 2021, 214 young women took part in the baseline study to assess their leadership skills. No Rise up trainings took place yet.

The total endline target for Palestine was lowered following the MTR, and is now set at 2,200 young women. Based on the actuals achieved so far, to reach the endline target in Palestine at least 556 young women should be trained in RiseUp! during 2024. It is expected there will be challenges in reaching this number, due to the circumstances in Gaza and West Bank

In 2024 YW4A continued with the Rise Up! Leaderships trainings for young women. The training topics were contextualized to align with national relevant issues, and the young women were actively engaged in safe spaces established by the YW4A partners. A total of 845 young women were trained in 2024, resulting in a total of 2,642 young women being engaged in RiseUp! Leadership programme throughout the years. While this is higher than the endline target of 2,200 young women, in Palestine their overall training attendance level is below expectation, partially due to the ongoing war and related heightened insecurity in the West Bank.In Palestine, the World YWCA conducted Psychological First Aid (PFA) training, equipping selected Trainer of Trainers with the skills needed to provide essential emotional and psychological support to survivors of GBV and establish referral pathways to governmental and non-governmental agencies. Through this training, young women were empowered as key change agents in their communities and they gained a deep understanding of their role in assisting fellow young women. Additionally, the training emphasized the importance of self-care and emotional well-being. Apart from Rise Up! and other training opportunities, the consortium prioritized initiatives to build young women's leadership skills and confidence through mentorship and platforms to engage with high-level decision-makers. For instance, young leaders were actively involved in various high-level forums, not just as participants but also as panelists and moderators. In 2024, they played key roles in platforms such as Beijing +30, the Human Rights Council 56th session (HRC), and the Sexual Violence Research Initiative (SVRI), showcasing their leadership and advocacy on global stages

Cohort 1 and 2 will cascade and train another cohort of 1070 young women (cohort 3). This target is different than the target presented in the Annual Plan 2022, as by accident the total YR5 target (4040 young women) was presented rather than the YR3 target. During the course of 2023, the target was adjusted upwards to 1,900.

In Palestine, under Pathway 2, the Rise Up! training aimed to enhance young women's leadership skills and empower them to become agents of change in their communities through advocacy initiatives and participation in local and international platforms, such as Women Deliver 2023. Trained young women also engaged in community initiatives, including producing short films on gender-based violence in Gaza, organizing solidarity events in the West Bank for Gazan women and children trapped in the West Bank, conducting theater performances and round table discussions on sexual harassment at workplaces, etc.The target for 2023 was adjusted upward following the MTR, to be 1,900 instead of 1,070, as Palestine had already exceeded the initial target of 1,070 by September 2023, reaching 1,172 participants. However, due to the unforeseen escalation of the war in Palestine in the 4th quarter, with the devastating war in Gaza and rising tension in the West Bank, the CL prioritized the safety and security of program staff and participants by transitioning physical activities and meetings to online platforms. As a result, the implementation of the Rise Up! training was temporarily withheld, and the target of 1,900 participants could not be met. Palestine achieved a total of 1,505 participants by the end of the year.
The initial target was set at 856 young women in 2022. Due to the deviation in the implementation during year 1, the target for 2022 was lowered to 240 young women.

Under Pathway 2, the YW4A programme enhances the leadership skills of young women through training and creating opportunities for them to train others and exercise their leadership, and be involved in advocacy. Throughout 2022, 292 young women were trained on the RiseUp! Leadership curriculum. Some of these young women have also participated in other trainings, for instance on legal and digital advocacy. The YW4A programme partners participated in various advocacy and dialogue spaces during the year, ensuring the involvement and active participation of young women and WROs.In 2021, the baseline targeted 214 young women; those young women later underwent RiseUp! Leadership training during 2022. During the year the partnerships were established with the WROs and the young women groups were identified. The programme design originally intended to target 2 cohorts of young women; cohort 1 (communities) and then cohort 2 (universities). That was changed, and alternately cohort 1 and 2 were engaged in parallel in 2022 following the adaptation of the RiseUp! training materials in a participatory way internally and with the young women and WROs. This decision was taken in order not to fall behind in the implementation. By 2022, the agreements were signed with the WROs and the training materials were adapted. By the end of the year, a total of 292 young women (230 in communities and 62 in universities) were trained in RiseUp.
The total endline target of 2,200 young women being trained in Rise Up! has been achieved, therefore no targets are set for 2025

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.1: (WRG045, WRG047) IO1 Enhanced capacity of 16-28 WROs to amplify young women's voices

description.narrative: Under IO1 YW4A focuses on enhancing the organizational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organisation. The programme also envisages amplifying young women’s voices by promoting that WROs provide space in their internal organisations for young women and establish internal inclusive processes and practices in decision-making, management, and programming. And by working with WROs to include, represent, hear, mentor, support, and prepare young women to take part in advocacy initiatives, link them to strategic decision-making forums, and scale-up local advocacy strategies.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.1 (WRG045): # of WROs with enhanced capacity to advance young women’s rights to bodily integrity and equal participation in decision-making.

description.narrative: Under IO1 YW4A focuses on enhancing the organisational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organsations through providing training.

comment.narrative: In Palestine YW4A targets a total of 6 WROs under IO1 (organisations with different types of leadership). In Y1 the advocacy and organisational capacity (AOCA) of the participating WROs was measured, as to set the baseline situation. In Palestine the WROs baseline AOCA capacity level is assessed as follows: 3 WROs at MODERATE capacity (1 WRG047, 2 WRG045), and 3 WROs at FAIR capacity (all 3 WRG045).

YW4A continues to work with the same WROs, including the organization that joined in 2022 (replacing an organization that dropped out). In 2023 a new organization in Gaza was identified (as a replacer) and onboarding started. However, due to the war between Hamas and Israel this was halted. In 2024 it was decided their engagement was no longer feasible, and the program in Palestine would focus on the remaining five WROs (all based in the West Bank).

Already back in 2023, the engagement of the Aisha Association - based in Gaza - came to a halt even before they could become actively engaged. In 2024, given the continuation of the war between Hamas and Israel, it became evident that there were no opportunities for the WRO to engage in the YW4A programme, and it was decided to focus on the five organizations based in the West Bank.YW4A continued to build the capacity of the five WROs in Palestine, through (refresher) digital and legal advocacy trainings, equipping young women and WROs with skills to engage policymakers effectively, and contributing to increased participation in legal and policy reforms for example on domestic violence, child marriage and SEAH policies. There was also strong emphasize on networking and coalition building, among other through participation in different regional coalitions, including the Hurra Coalition, to advocate for young women’s rights, policy and legal changes jointly with other organizations.
No deviations from targeted WROs

Capacity building activities with WROs in Y1 concerned: AGT 13 P/E/K/S Participatory design of M&E framework AP 1.1.1.4 Advocacy capacity assessment through workshops AP 1.1.1.6 Virtual workshop on the capacity assessment results on advocacy capacity and status of WRO partnership.

YW4A continues to work with the same WROs, including the WROs that replaced dropouts. During Q1, the partner in Gaza dropped out of the program. A new WRO was identified and onboarded as of August. However, since the start of the war between Hamas and Israel in Gaza their participation has been on-hold.

Capacity building continued throughout 2023, not only through trainings, but also through coalition building and joint advocacy efforts. The results from the AOCA mid-term assessment show progress among the four WROs that were involved in YW4A since the start. All four moved up one level on the AOCA scale compared to baseline, showing that 80% of the WROs that joined YW4A since 2021 have met YW4A’s IO1 target to move up one level or more on the AOCA scale. At mid-term the AOCA capacity level off the 5 involved WROs is: 2 WROs assessed at MODERATE capacity, and 3 at GOOD capacity.The re-assessment showed increased knowledge on YW4A topics and changes in the thinking of the AOCA core team compared to the baseline assessment. The capacity of the Palestinian WROs was mainly enhanced in terms of the WROs tactical advocacy skills and strategic advocacy, resulting from the digital and legal advocacy trainings led by partner Equality Now. There seemed to be lesser growth in the WROs organizational capacity so far, with the main focus of capacity building being on M&E and SEAH.
In 2022 YW4A is targeting the same 6 WROs as in 2021. One new WRO joined the programme as to replace a WRO that dropped out.

Throughout 2022, YW4A partners undertook activities to build all WROs’ advocacy and organisational capacity. For example, through training on legal and digital advocacy the targeted WROs in Palestine have increased their capacity. Building on legal capacity strengthening undertaken in the first year, partners have enhanced capacity to scale up the critical work they have been doing in addressing women’s rights issues and using their experiences to call for action from duty bearers through various advocacy initiatives in line with the YW4A advocacy priorities and the laws and policies targeted under IO4. They now have the required skills to supplement their legal advocacy campaigns with media strategies. This increased capacity to engage in legal advocacy can also be seen in the way WROs and young women are being strategic when engaging national processes and different policy makers and actors in their country. In Palestine, the six organisations targeted by YW4A (similar to Y1) took part in these activities. One of the WROs dropped out towards the end of the year. A new WRO has been identified and joined the programme.
During 2025, YW4A continues to target the same WOR's (those that take part since the start and new WROs that replaced initial selected WROs.
